newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan credit banks unveil bad loan disposal amount.
newsitem.headline: Japan credit banks unveil bad loan disposal amount.

text.p: Japan's three long-term credit banks on Monday disclosed the amount of problem loans they disposed of in the April-September first half of 1996/97.
The amounts were as follows, compared with the amount disposed of in the first half of 1995/96 (in billions of yen):
Of the banks' total problem loan disposals of 1.93 trillion yen in the 1995/96 full year, 856 billion yen came from IBJ, 650 billion yen from LCTB and 421.3 billion yen from Nippon Credit.

The banks disposed of problem loans by such measures as setting loan loss provisions, directly writing off bad loans, and selling such loans to the Cooperative Credit Purchasing Co Ltd (CCPC), a body set up by private-sector financial institutions.
The full names of the banks are Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ), Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd.
